assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gut-hormone physiology (GLP-1 insulinotropic action, proglucagon processing, receptor biology) translated into incretin drugs that now transform diabetes and obesity care and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Rare combination of mechanism, originality and very large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst supply the physiology and mechanism; Knudsen led the long-acting acylated analogue (liraglutide, semaglutide) program. Mojsov's and others' contributions to GLP-1 sequence and activity are contested and could make a three-person limit unfair.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and large outcome trials; clinical impact is established and timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen and non-listed early contributors is unresolved.
Industry-led drug development may be weighed differently from the underlying physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with synthetic receptors to treat cancer produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality; conceptually original and clinically decisive.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove CAR design (costimulation) and clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and gene-modified T cells. Chimeric receptor originators outside the credited list (e.g. Eshhar) are not available, complicating fairness.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation across centers; solid-tumor efficacy and safety limits remain, but the core achievement is mature.
uncertainties: Priority questions regarding the first chimeric receptor concept and who should share credit.
Long-term safety, secondary malignancies and limited solid-tumor success.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that ER stress is signaled to the nucleus through Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 splicing, defining the unfolded protein response, an organelle-to-nucleus communication pathway with broad relevance to disease. Clear, elegant, original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently delivered the decisive steps (Ire1 and mRNA splicing, Hac1/HAC1 mapping); the two-person configuration is clean and compact.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is firmly established and replicated for decades; disease links and therapeutic exploitation are still developing but do not affect the core discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee views the disease link as sufficient for Physiology or Medicine.
Recognition of other contributors (e.g. Ron, Ruddock) is not represented in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense modulation of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and a landmark for RNA-directed medicine; excellent bridge from RNA processing biology to patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target concept, Bennett led the antisense chemistry and clinical development; a coherent pair. Others (e.g. Singh, Hua, Gene Tools or Ionis colleagues) may have claims not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up; strongly validated and timely.
uncertainties: Role of related antisense chemistry and oligonucleotide pioneers who may deserve recognition.
Variable response by treatment timing and age.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and its role as a central nutrient-sensing controller of cell growth, with deep consequences for metabolism, aging, cancer and immunology; pivotal concept with broad impact and clinical rapalogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its function; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin chemical biology was key for the target. Sabatini's mTOR contributions are significant but omitted here; I do not rely on controversies I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Mature, extensively replicated and central in textbooks; clinical translation is more modest than the basic impact.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hall, Heitman/Movva, Schreiber, Sabatini, Sabers/Brown is difficult.
Clinical effectiveness of mTOR inhibitors is narrower than the biological significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term culture of Lgr5-positive adult stem cells as self-organizing organoids created a widely used platform for tissue biology, disease modeling and personalized medicine; strong originality and technology impact.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell identification and organoid concept; Sato executed the decisive culture work. A two-person credit looks fair, though Wnt and earlier 3D culture predecessors contribute context.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently reproduced; translational use in patient therapy and screening is still emerging, so timing is reasonably mature but not fully realized clinically.
uncertainties: Prior 3D culture and pluripotent-derived organoid work may complicate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned CML from a fatal disease into a manageable condition and established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy, building on the BCR-ABL oncogene history.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (chemistry and kinase inhibitor discovery), Druker (clinical translation) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. Earlier recognition of Rowley, Gallo and Baltimore-type work is a different matter.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of survival data; very strong confirmation, though possibly judged as already well recognized by other awards and as an extension of earlier oncogene discoveries.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as translational drug development rather than discovery of principle.
Tension between the three or more key contributors, including industry colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin and its use to control genetically defined neurons with light transformed neuroscience, enabling causal circuit dissection; original and widely transformative methodology.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins, Deisseroth established the neuronal application and tool development; Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims, so a three-person limit leaves unresolved omissions.
assessment.maturity: Extremely widely replicated; direct medicine impact is so far limited (early retinal clinical use), making it more tool than therapeutic discovery.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is the main obstacle with six credited names.
Whether a tool or technology fits Physiology or Medicine criteria.
